topic: Bluetooth is named after the Viking king Harald Bluetooth
taste: Rakesh: no object characters with faces in this one - real people (Harald, Vikings, the engineer) drawn as Style 5 humans. No horned helmets, no fighting.

claims.claim: Bluetooth is named after Harald 'Bluetooth' Gormsson, a 10th-century king of Denmark.
Harald was known for uniting Denmark and Norway.
In the 1990s Intel engineer Jim Kardach, who had been reading about Harald, proposed the name for a technology meant to unite PCs and mobile phones with a short-range wireless link.
The logo is a bind rune of Harald's initials: Hagall (H) and Bjarkan (B).
